introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch either a C or Pascal program development environment, and key in the corresponding program. Do not key in the line numbers, which have been provided for convenience. Compile the program. If any errors, keep correcting and compiling until the errors are all corrected. Save as Task 3.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a C or a Pascal development environment installed on the computer, create a new source file, key in the program of your choice **exactly as printed** without the line numbers, and compile it (*Build* / *Compile*, often F9). Save the file as **Task 3**.

- While typing, check the semicolons and braces in C, the `begin ... end.` and the `:=` in Pascal, the `&` before each variable in `scanf`, and the `%d` in the messages. Note that in Pascal there is no semicolon before `else`.
- If the compiler reports an error, go to the line indicated, correct it and compile again until there is no error.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* program keyed correctly (1); compiled without error (1); saved as Task 3 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Run the program three times with the inputs shown in the table below. Write in the space below, the last line on the screen in each case  *[3 marks]*

| | Birth Month | Birth Year | Current Month | Current Year |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First run | 10 | 2015 | 7 | 2020 |
| Second run | 4 | 2000 | 8 | 2015 |
| Third run | 6 | 2000 | 6 | 2020 |

First run: ................

Second run: ................

Third run: ................
questions.corrige_markdown:
The program tests the **month** first: if the birth month is less than or equal to the current month the birthday has been reached and age = current year - birth year; otherwise age = current year - birth year - 1. Then it displays a message according to the age. Trace (same logic simulated in Python):

| Run | bmonth <= cmonth ? | age | Message displayed |
|---|---|---|---|
| First (10, 2015, 7, 2020) | 10 <= 7: false | 2020 - 2015 - 1 = 4 | child (4 < 13) |
| Second (4, 2000, 8, 2015) | 4 <= 8: true | 2015 - 2000 = 15 | teen (12 < 15 < 20) |
| Third (6, 2000, 6, 2020) | 6 <= 6: true | 2020 - 2000 = 20 | adult (20 > 19) |

- First run: **Hello child, you are 4 years old.**
- Second run: **Hello teen, you are 15 years old.**
- Third run: **Hello adult, you are 20 years old.**

Only one of the three messages is displayed each time, because the three tests (age < 13, 12 < age < 20, age > 19) never hold together.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* one mark per correct line.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain what the program is designed to do.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The program asks for a person's **birth month and year** and for the **current month and year**, calculates the person's **age in complete years** (it subtracts one year if the birth month has not yet been reached this year), and then displays a message that depends on the age: **child** for an age under 13, **teen** for an age from 13 to 19, and **adult** for an age of 20 or more, together with the age.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* computes the age from the dates (1); displays child / teen / adult according to the age (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Re-write the second if statement (line 17 of the C program, or line 18 of the pascal program) but this time use the >= 13 and <= 19 instead of the > 12 and < 20 operators respectively. What can you say about the outputs when you run the program again using the same inputs as in (2)  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
New statements:

```c
if ((age >= 13) && (age <= 19))
```

```pascal
if ((age >= 13) and (age <= 19)) then
```

**The outputs are exactly the same** as before. Age is a whole number (an integer), so `age > 12` means the same as `age >= 13`, and `age < 20` means the same as `age <= 19`: the two conditions select the same ages (13 to 19). With the three sets of inputs the program still displays the child message (age 4), the teen message (age 15) and the adult message (age 20). (Checked with Python for every whole age from -5 to 199: both versions select the same messages.)

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the statement correctly rewritten (1); same outputs, with the reason (integer age) (1).
